title: Catalog API pagination contract decision
purpose: Document two competing Catalog API pagination drafts and the unresolved authoritative contract selection.

scope.text: Catalog API pagination has two competing drafts: draft A uses a JSON object with items and next_cursor; draft B uses a top-level JSON array with page and page_size.

requirements.text: GET /v1/items returns a JSON object with an items array and next_cursor string.
UI must support moving to the next page.
GET /v1/items returns a top-level JSON array and uses page and page_size query parameters.

stories.text: If a human selects draft A, a client can retrieve catalog items from GET /v1/items as a JSON object with an items array and next_cursor string, and the UI can move to the next page.
acceptance_criteria: Given a human has selected draft A, when GET /v1/items succeeds, then the response is a JSON object containing an items array and a next_cursor string.
Given a human has selected draft A and a next_cursor string is present in the response, when the user triggers the next-page action, then the UI requests the next page and displays it.

stories.text: If a human selects draft B, a client can retrieve catalog items from GET /v1/items as a top-level JSON array using page and page_size query parameters.
acceptance_criteria: Given a human has selected draft B, when GET /v1/items succeeds, then the response is a top-level JSON array.
Given a human has selected draft B, when a client sends page and page_size query parameters, then the endpoint accepts those parameters and returns a top-level JSON array.

dependencies.text: Neither draft is approved; the authoritative contract has not been selected.
Implementation of either draft depends on a human selecting the corresponding contract as authoritative.

risks.text: Selecting draft A would fail draft B's requested top-level JSON array and page/page_size behavior; selecting draft B would fail draft A's requested JSON object and next_cursor behavior.
Implementing both contracts without a selection would create incompatible client expectations.

success_metrics.text: A client can retrieve catalog items and navigate pages using the selected contract.

open_questions: Which Catalog API draft should a human select as authoritative: draft A or draft B?
Who has authority to select the authoritative contract?
What are the required, default, and maximum values for page and page_size in draft B?
How should draft A's next_cursor be generated and encoded?
